video_title: Pressured To Sell?? Dave McMenamin On The Lakers Sale to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner -Sedano + Kap

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: Questions regarding the Lakers' power structure after the sale
quotes.excerpt: What does this mean for Jeanie Buss, Rob Pelinka, Lon Rosen, the current power structure?

text_blocks.speaker: Dave McMenamin
text_blocks.text: This gets a lot of questions right now. Questions that I am asking sources, and people around the league are asking me. What does this mean for Jeanie Buss, Rob Pelinka, Lon Rosen, the current power structure that's with the organization? That's been asked to me by several people and I don't know yet.

text_blocks.speaker: Jorge Sedano
text_blocks.text: So glad you're bringing this up, because here's the thing. When we get on the air at 7:00 a.m. and we find this news out, for us, we go into breaking news mode and we start trying to figure out why would you do something like this?

text_blocks.speaker: Kap
text_blocks.text: On one hand, $2 billion in a year, that's an amazing return on investment. But on the other hand, there is this investigation. Could this investigation into Mark Walter have forced his hand?

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter's potential motivations for selling the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: Is this just him seeing an opportunity to make a quick $2 billion?

text_blocks.speaker: Dave McMenamin
text_blocks.text: What's really going on with Mark Walter? Obviously, we've seen the reporting in the LA Times about the SEC investigation into his businesses. Is this just him seeing an opportunity to make a quick $2 billion and, geez, how can you besmirch someone for that opportunity, I guess? But if the Lakers is some legacy brand and one of the greatest things you can invest in, is a quick $2 billion really that special, or is it because he needed the money for his other businesses?

text_blocks.speaker: Kap
text_blocks.text: Could this investigation into Mark Walter have forced his hand? Perhaps even maybe the leak says to him, 'We don't like this, you're one of our new owners, we don't like this, this is bad news for us, we're ready for you to get in and get out.'

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: Andrew Friedman's involvement in the Lakers front office
quotes.excerpt: Andrew Friedman is one of the smartest executives in sports. He is the president of the Dodgers.

text_blocks.speaker: Jorge Sedano
text_blocks.text: I'm a big fan of Andrew Friedman. I think he's one of the smartest executives in sports. He is the president of the Dodgers. He had some level of involvement in at least overseeing kind of what the Lakers front office was up to most recently. Do you think there's at least a slither of a possibility that they looked at this situation and said, 'Maybe Walter goes to Friedman and says, 'Hey Andrew, can we make this like Dodgers 2.0?''

text_blocks.speaker: Dave McMenamin
text_blocks.text: I'd be surprised if that was the main thrust. But over the course of those 14 months, of course we know that the CBA for Major League Baseball is completely different than the NBA. I believe that he is very good at his job, obviously he's proven in the pudding with what he's done with the Dodgers. But it never quite meshed in my brain that, 'Oh, because we have success in one sport, we can replicate that structure in another sport.'

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers' need to hire a second assistant general manager
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers still haven't hired that second assistant general manager that Rob Pelinka said he planned to hire.
quotes.quote: With the supposed infusion of cash, the Lakers still haven't hired that second assistant general manager that Rob Pelinka said he planned to hire at the beginning of the off-season. If they had the requisite number for a while around, I'm pretty sure that person would be in place. I don't know if it was just a blank check after blank check after blank check that they were providing to the Lakers organization since taking over.

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' opening night against the Golden State Warriors
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers having opening night against Golden State doesn't quite have the same pizzazz.
quotes.quote: The Lakers having opening night against Golden State doesn't quite have the same pizzazz that it had the last few years where you have LeBron versus Steph. I guess per a Laker fan, it's a more winnable game than maybe some of the other teams that you could be put up against to begin the season, especially because Golden State is not going to have Jimmy Butler or Moses Moody to begin the season.

quotes.speaker: Dave McMenamin
quotes.summary_phrase: JJ Redick's challenge coaching a new Lakers roster
quotes.excerpt: JJ Redick has done a great job the last two years with different iterations of the team.
quotes.quote: JJ Redick has done a great job the last two years with different iterations of the team because of injuries or trades. This year, he's got to do a great job with a basically entirely new roster. This is probably going to be the most important year of his coaching career, because if he gets this team going in the right direction, you're building something for years to come. If this team struggles, where are the levers to improve them? That's the big question mark when you make that trade for Walker Kessler and commit all those assets to do it.
